title: Counterexamples to weak chromatic splitting: sphere kernels and descent exponents
main_claim: For p>=5 the canonical weak chromatic splitting map i_{p,X}: L_{p-1}S_p -> L_{p-1}L_{K(p)}S_p has no homotopy retraction, and for p>=7 the same holds for i_{p+1,X}. The witness is z_p = beta_1^{(p-1)^2}. Its image in L_{p-1}S_p is nonzero, because it is detected in E_{p-1}^{hG} by the Hopkins-Miller/Heard computation. Its image in L_{K(a)}S is zero for a = p or p+1, because of the horizontal vanishing line. A second, independent proof at height p compares descent exponents: exp_H(E_{p-1}) > p^2+2 >= exp_H(T(B_p)).
sibling_notes: This paper is consistent with the family-318 sibling reports. The other papers in the family refute strong chromatic splitting (CSC) at height 3. This one refutes the weak form, using the completed sphere, at heights p (p>=5) and p+1 (p>=7). The argument is short given Heard's E_inf computation for E_{p-1}^{hG}: beta_1^{(p-1)^2} is nonzero at height p-1, and it lies in filtration above the vanishing line at height p, where S_p has no p-torsion. A specialist should confirm that Heard Lemma 5.8 states beta^{h^2} != 0 in E_inf exactly as used here.
